To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a self report scale (SAIQ) was more strongly associated with a researcher rated scale (SUMD) when administered first than when it was administered second.
the SUMD and the SAIQ are not interchangeable measures of insight, and that a self report measure should be administered before a clinician-rated measure.
the SUMD and the SAIQ are significantly correlated in the SAI Q first group but not the SUMD first.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity of self-report scales of insight in schizophrenia.

the relationship between the researcher rated Scale to Assess Unawarement of Mental Disorder and the self report Self Appraisal of Illusion Questionnaire in a sample of patients with chronic schizophrenia.
the development and testing of a self report measure of insight, the SAIQ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a researcher rated insight scale should not be used in isolation to assess insight in schizophrenia.
the SAIQ is a valid and reliable self report measure of insight in chronic schizophrenia.
the SUMD and the SAIQ are both valid instruments for the assessment of insight in schizophrenia, but their validity is affected by the order of administration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the order of administration of insight scales may affect validity.
self report scales may be a valid and reliable measure of insight in schizophrenia, but only if administered first in a counterbalanced design.
a self report insight measure is more likely to be valid when the self report is administered prior to the researcher rated scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-report measure of insight should be administered first.
researchers should be aware of the potential impact of order of administration on the results of their insight research.
researchers and clinicians should consider order of administration when evaluating insight.
